issues.description: Element: interface used for riding animals (method messageOnRide()). Problem statement and template refer to an interface named Rideable with abstract method messageOnRide(). The solution repository, however, defines an interface named Mountable (with messageOnRide()) and leaves Rideable.java empty; Pig and Seal implement Mountable rather than Rideable. This naming mismatch between Rideable and Mountable will confuse students and can cause compilation errors or test integration failures because the template and tests expect Rideable while the solution code uses Mountable.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the ride interface name and usages consistent across all artifacts. Option A (preferred): rename Mountable to Rideable in the solution (file Mountable.java -> Rideable.java), remove or replace the empty Rideable.java, and have Pig and Seal implement Rideable. Ensure the Rideable interface declares String messageOnRide(). Option B: update the problem statement and template to refer to Mountable instead of Rideable and ensure tests reference Mountable. Ensure exactly one interface with the method signature messageOnRide() is present and used consistently by all classes and tests.

issues.description: The exercise describes and references an interface named 'Rideable' (problem_statement.md and the template's Main.java), but the solution implementation defines and uses an interface named 'Mountable' (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Mountable.java) and has an empty Rideable.java file (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Rideable.java). Specifically: the problem statement defines interface 'Rideable' with messageOnRide() (problem_statement.md lines 47-49); the template Main.java references Rideable in the example usage (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java lines 23-24). In the solution, Pig.java (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Pig.java line 3) and Seal.java (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java line 4) implement 'Mountable' instead of 'Rideable', and Rideable.java in the solution is empty (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Rideable.java line 1). This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual entity (an interface for animals that can be ridden) prevents a clear mapping between the problem requirements and the solution/template code, and will confuse or block students who implement/expect 'Rideable' while the provided solution uses 'Mountable'.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier across all artifacts. Preferred fix: rename the solution's Mountable interface to Rideable (move/rename Mountable.java -> Rideable.java) and update implementing classes (Seal.java, Pig.java) to 'implements Rideable'. Remove or replace the empty Rideable.java in the solution so there is a single Rideable interface declaring String messageOnRide(). Alternatively, if you prefer 'Mountable' as the canonical name, update the problem statement and template references to 'Mountable' and ensure the interface declares messageOnRide(). Ensure consistency so students can map the requirement to the code and tests without confusion.
